items.text: Žalgiris play at about 87 possessions a game, Kretinga 76. Žalgiris score **1.48 per possession when the shot comes in the first 8 seconds** and only 0.78 when they have to attack a set defence after a made basket. Kretinga's plan writes itself: good shots, get back, make Žalgiris play half court.
items.title: The pace fight

items.text: Kretinga allow 1.12 points per possession after an opponent's defensive rebound, against 0.91 after their own made basket. Against the league's fastest-finishing team, **a long Kretinga miss is half a Žalgiris layup**. Watch how many Kretinga players crash and how many sprint back.
items.title: Kretinga's misses feed the break

items.text: Urbonas averages 39 of 40 minutes, Einikis 35, Goriunovas and Adomaitis 32. Žalgiris roll nine or ten players. Kretinga have won Q3 by +14 over three games but Q4 by only +3. **If Žalgiris keep the pace up, the last eight minutes are where depth shows.**
items.title: Four Kretinga starters barely sit

items.text: Kretinga take 13% of their shots from the corners (league 6%) and make 48%. Žalgiris almost never give that shot up (5% of shots against them). **Whoever wins the corners wins Kretinga's half court**: if Žalgiris's helpers stay home, Kretinga must score at the rim, where Žalgiris allow 52%.
items.title: The corner three

items.text: Urbonas is 14/30 from three and scores 1.35 points per shot. Einikis takes as many shots (47) at 0.85, mostly drives, 2/16 from three. **A Žalgiris plan: top-lock Urbonas, go under screens for Einikis** and wall off the paint behind him.
items.title: Who takes Kretinga's shots

items.text: In the four possessions before a Žalgiris timeout they have been outscored 25–47 this season; in the four after, 31–33. **This bench uses timeouts to reset, and it works.** On the other side, Gasiūnas (+61 per 100 on court) and Grenda (+44) are the defence-first players whose minutes matter most.
items.title: Žalgiris's timeouts stop runs
items.evidence: on/off samples ~170 possessions each, three games

items.text: Team sheets are in. Žalgiris are without **#4 Gasiūnas**, whose minutes had their best defensive numbers, so watch who Bardauskas trusts at the point of attack. Kretinga dress only nine, with #33 Mažeikis new to the rotation: on top of four starters who already play 32+ minutes, the pace question gets sharper.
items.evidence: Gasiūnas: Žalgiris allowed 68 per 100 with him on, 98 off (167 poss). Kretinga roster: 9 listed.

items.text: Mikaločius opens with his usual five, the group that is **slightly negative over a big sample** this season. Its problem is spacing: Bružas and Adomaitis both live in the paint, so Einikis drives into two bodies. The same four with Paulauskas, a pure shooter, have been clearly better.
items.evidence: Usual five: −5 per 100 over 168 poss. With Paulauskas for Bružas: +25 over 55. Paulauskas 7/18 from three, 0% of shots inside

items.text: **Push off every miss and every steal.** Žalgiris score 1.48 per possession early in the clock and 0.78 against a set defence.
items.evidence: Season: 149 early-clock possessions at 1.48; 98 after opponent scores at 0.78

items.text: **Two back on every shot.** Kretinga's long misses are Žalgiris's best offence; win the pace and the half court is yours.
items.evidence: Kretinga allow 1.12 per possession after a defensive rebound, 0.91 after a make

items.text: Kretinga's first points are an Einikis three, exactly the shot the Žalgiris scout wants him taking. One make doesn't change the bet: **going under on Einikis and staying attached to Urbonas** is still right, as long as Žalgiris don't overreact and start chasing him over screens.
items.evidence: Einikis 2/16 from three in three earlier games; Urbonas 14/30
